> Nope.

True Faith's text does not say anything about "strikes against" this
minion:

Put this card on a non-infernal mortal ally you control, or pay 2 pool to
put this card on any non-infernal minion you control. Actions requiring
Dominate [dom] or Presence [pre] cannot be directed at this minion. In
combat, any damage this minion inflicts on an infernal minion is
aggravated. Infernal minions cannot block or strike this minion. Burn
this card if this minion becomes infernal.

Maybe what you're referring to is "cannot...strike this minion", but I
think that's different from what I'm asking.
The specific word "against" is what is causing me to ask the question.

As English is full of ambiguities, the sentence on Lucian could be
interpreted as:

Strikes, when in combat against Lucian, cost an additional blood or life.

or

Strikes that do something to Lucian cost an additional blood or life.

Messages.Author: brandons...@yahoo.com
Messages.Body:
On May 20, 12:06 pm, Jozxyqk <jfeue...@eecs.tufts.edu> wrote:


Sometimes you have to act like a lawyer in order to parse what card
text means. That terms are different may be a red flag, indicating a
subtle difference, or it could be nothing. Defining terms is, in my
opinion, the most crucial part of an argument or statement. Secret
Library lists 1,973 different library cards and 1,288 different crypt
cards by my count(aside from the new set). How can one be expected to
memorize not only card text, but errata to each one of these? Does it
hurt to ask for a point of clarification when new cards come out or
when issues arise? Even if said issue has been addressed before, at
worst you get an entry in the archive linking "lucian" and "strike
against" for future reference.

Like Jozxyqk, I wasn't clear what was implied by "Strikes against

Lucian cost and additional blood or life."

Clarification 1: Would this be any strike? If so, it might be better
to write "when in combat with Lucian, strikes cost an additional blood
or life."
Answer: No, not any strike.

Clarification 2: What sort of strikes qualify as being "strikes
against Lucian?"
Possible answer: Strikes that target Lucian with an effect and/or
damage. Strike: Go to torpor Strike: Dodge and Hand strike(one strike)
Strike: Combat ends and inflict 1 damage, etc. Things this would not
count as "strikes against," would be Strike: Dodge or Combat Ends,
Strike: Prevent two damage from the next hand or melee weapon strike,
Strike: Equip... Possible gray area: Strikes that have no direct
effect at long range, but grant a press (i.e. Lamb Into at vic), some
strike that adds a counter but does not inflict damage, Strike:
Destroy equipment (targets equipment, not minion), Strike: hands for
10 targeting a retainer, Strike: hand strike (at zero strength),
Strike: Hand strike. Damage from this strike is reduced to zero.

The list goes on and I've only been playing since LotN, so maybe more
experienced players can think of more. This is a clean slate and I,
like (I assume) Jozxyqk, try to be a good player and understand the
rules. Having this conversation is good, it makes effects more clear
and anyone who looks at it can go to a draft and say "I know exactly
what that special means."

Sincerely,
Brandon

So, then, LSJ, what are you saying is the definition of "strikes

superior? Strikes that are known to be ineffective such as hand
strikes at range?

- D.J.

Do the guys who made this article understand anything about VTES ???
